/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: DERIVE_FROM_REPO
Q3: A
Q4: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: The `retrigger_review` branch (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` lines 19979-20023) only works through `_resolve_issue_implementation_pr "${issue_num}"`, so an issue-less PR cannot use it without changing that action's contract. Options B and C both reshape it, and B also moves the PR head, which would invalidate the marker's `head=` match. `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` (line 27211) already dispatches by PR number from the default branch only (the #4701 security fix). It already has the cycle-local dedupe and the `_has_active_autofix_run` in-flight guard, and its rc=2 maps directly to `outcome=in_flight`. This is the same "reuse the existing re-queue path" the issue intends under §6.
Q2: Neither option holds up as written, so the answer comes from the repo. A reuses `N_COMMENTS_JSON`, but the noop loop skips that fetch for every PR the batch marked `_STANDALONE_NOOP_CLEAR_PRS` (line 35293). That covers every PR with no "Editor no-op suspicious" warning, which is exactly the `reviewers_failed` / `provider_unavailable` case, so A would miss most candidates. B adds a second batch of comments for the same PRs, against §14 "check first, add second". The conflict sweep already sends one GraphQL alias batch per 30 PRs (lines 34813-34865) with `comments(last: 100)` and author logins. Extending those same aliases costs no new calls.
Q3: `_noop_cap_review_support_sha` (lines 35190-35208) resolves the review-support SHA from local data only (`ORCHESTRATOR_ENGINE_SHA` in coding-workflows, the `review_autofix.yml@<40-hex>` pin elsewhere). This is the pin that will actually run the retry, so it is the only reading that meets Goal 2's "do not re-run into the same crash". Option B can retry on an unsynced consumer pin and repeat the crash.
Q4: The noop sweep already applies the #7126 rules: a same-repository head (lines 35279-35287, failing closed on unknown) and markers counted only from `unblock_trusted_login` (lines 35343-35350). Anyone can open a fork PR or paste a marker comment, so option B would let an outsider trigger privileged review dispatches.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 34771-34778: the `STANDALONE_PRS` snapshot (number, headRefName, headRefOid, isDraft, isCrossRepository, headRepositoryOwner).
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 34813-34865: the existing 30-PR GraphQL alias batch. Each alias already requests `state headRefOid isDraft comments(last: 100) { pageInfo { hasPreviousPage } nodes { body databaseId author { login } } }`.
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 22260 `_fetch_standalone_pipeline_label_issues_graphql`: the source of the pipeline label set that counts as a "linked pipeline issue".
    - scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py lines 4796-4815: the marker format `<!-- review-autofix-failure:v1 head=<40hex> reason=<tok> fp=<hex> degraded=<0|1> [run=<n>] [support=<40hex>] -->`. `support=` is optional.
  steps:
    - Add two fields to each alias of the existing batch at line 34828: `closingIssuesReferences(first: 10) { totalCount nodes { number labels(first: 30) { nodes { name } } } }` and `labels(first: 30) { nodes { name } }`. The batch size, the call count (ceil(N/30)) and the fail-open handling stay as they are. Update the batch's input/output/call-count comment (lines 34798-34802) to name the new outputs.
    - Inside the existing per-PR `while` loop (lines 34836-34863), fill a new cycle-local associative array named so it does not collide with any existing name (for example `_STANDALONE_ISSUELESS_RETRY_STATE`). Store one compact JSON value per PR: head OID, whether it is linked to a pipeline issue, whether it has the `ai:review-blocked` label, the newest failure-marker fields, and the retry-marker keys present. Fill it only when the alias node validates with the same checks as lines 34840-34841: the number, head ref and OID match the list, and the PR is OPEN.
    - Count a PR as "linked" (and therefore excluded) when any closing reference carries a label from the `_fetch_standalone_pipeline_label_issues_graphql` set. If `totalCount` is larger than the number of nodes returned, also treat it as linked (fail closed).
    - Parse markers only from comments whose `author.login` equals `UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN`. If the login is unresolved, record nothing (fail closed, matching line 35348).
    - Add one function that reads this map, called once per cycle after the standalone stall pass (and after the noop sweep). For each same-repository, non-draft, unlinked PR without `ai:review-blocked` whose newest trusted non-retry-marker comment carries a `review-autofix-failure:v1` marker, check the marker: `head` must equal the current head OID and `reason` must be in {reviewers_failed, provider_unavailable, sandbox_prepare_failed}. Then apply the gates in this order: support SHA (Q3), already_retried, the per-cycle cap, and dispatch (Q1).
    - Because the retry marker is posted after the failure comment, a 100-comment window that contains the failure marker also contains any later retry marker, so `already_retried` stays accurate when `hasPreviousPage` is true.
    - If a batch fails, its PRs simply have no map entry: log `ISSUELESS_REVIEW_RETRY outcome=skipped reason=prefetch_unavailable` once per cycle and let the rest of the cycle run unchanged.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "a new `_fetch_issueless_review_retry_candidates_graphql` batch (50 per alias batch, last 5 comments)" (Approach step 1 / Constraints §15)
  equivalence_argument: The data is the same (closing references with labels, recent comments with authors, head SHA, draft and open state) and it comes from a batch already sent once per cycle with documented fail-open behaviour. The pass makes no extra read calls instead of ceil(N/50). The window is 100 comments instead of 5, which is a superset of what the issue asked for. The `updated within ISSUELESS_REVIEW_RETRY_MAX_AGE_DAYS` filter can still be applied to the batch data if `updatedAt` is added to the same alias. The default of 7 is kept.
  reversibility: The added alias fields and the new map are additive. With `ISSUELESS_REVIEW_RETRY_MAX_PER_CYCLE=0` the pass only logs. If a reviewer later wants a separate helper, the selection function reads from one map and can be fed by a dedicated batch without changing the gate or act logic.

Notes for the planner (they follow from the decisions above and are binding):
- Q1: call `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts "<pr>" "<head_ref>"`. rc=0 posts the trusted `<!-- issueless-review-retry:v1 head=<40hex> support=<40hex> -->` marker and logs `outcome=retriggered`. rc=2 logs `outcome=in_flight` and posts no marker. rc=1 logs `outcome=skipped reason=dispatch_failed` and posts no marker. Leave `retrigger_review` unchanged and rename nothing.
- Q3: call `_noop_cap_review_support_sha` once. If `NOOP_CAP_REVIEW_SUPPORT_STATE` is not `ok`, log `outcome=skipped reason=support_unresolved`. If the marker has no `support=` field, it cannot be compared, so log `outcome=skipped reason=marker_support_missing` (fail closed). If the marker's support equals the resolved SHA, log `outcome=waiting_for_release`.
- Q4: apply the same-repository head check from lines 35279-35287 and fail closed on unknown or missing fields. Use the trusted login for reading both marker families and for posting the retry marker.

None of these decisions needs a placeholder secret or variable, so there is no SETUP REQUIRED section.
